_note: Starter glossaries for the DialekKita dialect layer. Native speakers: please verify and extend. Each glossary pair is [dialect word, standard Bahasa Malaysia]. Each example pair is [dialect sentence, standard Bahasa Malaysia sentence].

kelantan.name: Kelantanese Malay (Kecek Kelate)
kelantan.style: Spoken Kelantanese. Vowel endings often shift (-a to -o, e.g. dua -> duo, tiga -> tigo, mana -> mano). Final -ah often becomes -oh (rumah -> ghumoh). 'r' is often written 'gh'.
examples: Paip ghumoh ambo bocor doh duo ari.
Paip rumah saya bocor sudah dua hari.

utara.name: Northern Malay (Kedah / Penang / Perlis)
utara.style: Spoken northern Malay. Final -ar/-ir often written -aq/-iq (pasar -> pasaq). Final -s often -ih (habis -> habih).
examples: Cek nak habaq, lif blok B rosak.
Saya hendak beritahu, lif blok B rosak.

sabah.name: Sabah Malay
sabah.style: Spoken Sabah Malay. The particle 'bah' adds emphasis or agreement and should be kept when writing in Sabah Malay.
examples: Sia ndak tau mana pejabat pengurusan.
Saya tidak tahu di mana pejabat pengurusan.

sarawak.name: Sarawak Malay
examples: Saya mahu pergi ke klinik sekarang.

manglish.name: Manglish (Malaysian colloquial English)
manglish.style: Malaysian colloquial English mixing English with Malay words and particles such as lah, lor, meh, kan.
examples: Boss, check pass kejap, after that can enter.
Sila tunjukkan pas pelawat, kemudian boleh masuk.
Aircon spoil already lah, can send people fix or not?
Penghawa dingin sudah rosak, boleh hantar orang untuk baiki?
Got parcel for me or not?
